QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_9

question.text: Satluj Infrastructure AIF (Cat I, 10-year close-ended) nears end-of-tenure with two unliquidated assets. Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, the maximum period for which the fund tenure (not Large Value Fund) can be extended, and the required consent threshold, are:

answer.text: Up to 1 year, with simple majority (>50%) of unit-holders by value
Up to 2 years, with two-thirds of unit-holders by value of their investment
Up to 3 years, with 75% of unit-holders by value of their investment
Up to 5 years automatically; no investor consent needed

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 13(5) / CTR guidance permits a close-ended AIF to extend tenure by up to 2 YEARS with approval from 2/3rd of unit-holders by VALUE of their investment. Large Value Funds for Accredited Investors may extend up to 5 years under the 2024 amendment. The Trap: 1 year / simple majority understates both period and threshold. 3 years / 75% confuses with the liquidation in-specie consent (75%). 5-year automatic is LVF-specific and still requires 2/3rd LVF approval. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B test the 2/3rd threshold. XIX-C expects knowledge of the LVF carve-out for 5-year extension via 2024 amendment.
